chapter: Russell's band, records and Armstrong in the studio
title: The January 1929 Okeh sessions and the tuba players
summary: They made 'Savoy Shout', 'Call of the Freaks' and 'Tight Like That' under Russell's name; Holmes recalls Bass Moore and Pops Foster both being on the date.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Now, after that some records were made on January...
1928? Or was it '29?
Yeah, it would have to be '29. Yeah, on January '29 for Okeh...
Okeh Records.
Okeh Records. And these were now issued under Russell's name.
Do you have the titles of any of them?
Yeah. "Savoy Shout," "Call of the Freaks" and "Tight Like That."
That's right. They were under...?
They were issued under Russell's name as Luis Russell and His Burning Eight.
But it was really King Oliver's date. But the records were under Russell's name.
Well, let me play one of those now.
[PLAYS MUSIC ("Savoy Shout"?)]
Well, you were much more in your element there.
Yeah, that goes back a way. Let me see, that was a soprano saxophone. That was not a clarinet.
No, that was an alto sax.
Was it alto?
Yeah, that was an alto.
I know it was a saxophone. It wasn't a clarinet.
Now, there was a tuba on that record.
I know. And I was trying to think who it was,.
In the books it's...
I know it was Moore or....
It's listed as Moore.
It must be Moore, then.
It's listed as Bass Moore. So that these are then before Russell could have sent for...
Well, it is before he started...
Before he got Pops Foster.

Well, could be. But I know that one of the bass... When Pops was there, he still had tuba there, too. Both of them were there. Pops Foster had just come in, you know, and both of them were there on the same date. Yeah, Moore and Pops -- Pops Foster. See, he was getting a band together. That was what you might say the original band there. Then Pops moved in. And then the rest of them came behind... Like, Simeon came I think next, and he was in the
band a while, and ...(?)., and Paul Barbarin came in.
